holidays.name: National Sugar Cookie Day
holidays.description: A day for rolling, cutting, frosting and sprinkling. Bakers of every skill level can turn butter, sugar and flour into edible art. Cookie cutters and a heavy hand with the sprinkles are encouraged.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance, and its exact origin is unclear. It has become a yearly favorite among bakers and sweet-tooth fans.
holidays.funFact: Many food historians trace sugar cookies to German settlers in Pennsylvania, who baked them in the 1700s. Sugar cookies were later named the official cookie of Pennsylvania.

holidays.name: National Don't Put All Your Eggs in One Omelet Day
holidays.description: A cheeky food holiday that takes the old proverb about not keeping all your eggs in one basket and puts it in a frying pan. It is a day to spread your breakfast bets, whether that means a few small omelets or a different egg dish.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It plays on the proverb about diversifying your risks.
holidays.funFact: The proverb about eggs and baskets is centuries old. It appeared in Cervantes' Don Quixote in the early 1600s.

holidays.name: Fashion Day
holidays.description: A day to dress up, try a bold new look and celebrate style in all its forms. Wear the loud socks, the statement hat or the outfit you have been saving for a special occasion.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It encourages people to express themselves through clothing.
holidays.funFact: The word fashion comes from the Old French word facon, meaning make or shape. It began as a word for how something is made, not for what people wear.
